commits.message: A held widget paints no overlay, pinned with the terminal wide enough to show one (rich-widgets-hmk1.kvc)

Tab from a widget held on no column moves to its neighbour in document order; review fixes (rich-widgets-hmk1.kvc)

The focus manager reads the view's document order and its on-screen widgets
from one FocusView, so settle takes no argument and next/prev step from the
current widget's place in the view rather than its place on screen.

Also: Panel's and Table's moved JSDocs back onto their members, one cellAt for
Table's blank-cell fallback, Composite says it commits no state rather than
that it is pure, and contents.test holds Table without its header and Tree with
its root hidden.

A widget its container hands no column is held in the view, not drawn, so it keeps focus and nothing renders for it (rich-widgets-hmk1.kvc)

protocol's render is the one reporter of what the view holds: RenderOptions.onDraw,
called by WidgetBase, becomes onPresent(renderable, "drawn" | "held"), called by
render for every renderable it is asked for. Under one column a renderable is held:
render walks the Composite.contents() of what it holds, reports each held, and
renders nothing, so a Viewport's offset or a TextInput's scroll window is never
committed at a width that is not shown.

Every exported container implements Composite. The method is contents(), not the
children() the seam named, because Tree.children and Layout.children are already
Rich's names for subtrees and panes. test/renderables/contents.test.ts holds each
exported renderable's contents() to what its render draws.

WidgetApp settles focus over the widgets the frame holds, drawn or held, and exposes
them as WidgetApp.present.

A widget its container hands no column keeps focus, as one the frame crops does (rich-unfiled-791c.pf3y)

Under one column protocol's render draws nothing, as Rich's Console.render
does, and so never reached the widgets inside: FocusManager.settle saw a
widget squeezed out of its pane as gone from the view and moved focus to the
first one. Now render still tells onDraw of the owners a renderable handed no
column holds, by drawing it at one column and dropping the output, and only
when someone listens.

Every child is drawn through protocol's render, so one handed no column draws nothing, as under Rich's Console.render (rich-unfiled-791c.wyrk) (#470)

* Every child is drawn through protocol's render, so one handed no column draws nothing, as under Rich's Console.render (rich-unfiled-791c.wyrk)

render(renderable, options) in src/core/protocol.ts is the one place the
under-one-column rule is kept; every src/ call of a Renderable's render goes
through it, and test/seam/render-calls.test.ts fails on one that does not.
The drawsNothing checks in Padding, Panel, Table, Traceback and Markdown are
gone. Tree no longer holds a row for a label that drew nothing, as Rich's
does not. squeezed-child.golden.json pins Rich 15's rows for Padding, Panel,
Constrain, Tree, Layout and Markdown at a width that leaves the child none.

* render is exported and the protocol page draws children through it; the render-calls gate sees an optional-chained receiver (rich-unfiled-791c.wyrk review)

* An empty block placed by Align draws no row, pinned against Rich 15 (rich-unfiled-791c.wyrk review)

* A tree label that draws nothing has no row, as Rich 15's; the comment no longer says only a squeezed one (rich-unfiled-791c.wyrk review)
